Application Materials.content:
You will be asked to submit the following documents in order for your application to be considered:
| Document | Required | Details |
|---|---:|---|
| Personal Statement | Yes | A personal statement is required. This can be entered directly into the online application form (**maximum 4,000 characters**) or uploaded as an attachment to the online application form (**maximum 2 pages**). |
| Previous Academic Study | Yes | A copy (or copies) of your official academic transcript(s), showing the subjects studied and marks obtained. If you have already completed your degree, copies of your official degree certificate will also be required. Applicants with academic documents issued in a language other than English, will need to submit both the original and official translation of their documents. |
| References | Yes | One academic reference is required. A professional reference will be accepted if you have completed your qualifications over five years ago. In some cases, we may request an additional reference from you. |
| Other | Optional | Applicants may wish to include a CV (Resume) or evidence of professional registration as part of their application. |

Interview Requirements.content: Some of King’s courses require students to attend an interview in order to assess qualities which might be harder to assess from the application form, or where an applicant is offering non-traditional qualifications. If a course uses interviews as part of the selection process, this does not mean that all applicants will be asked to attend an interview. If invited to an interview, applicants will be provided with further details and guidance.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **UK applicants:** A minimum high 2:1 undergraduate Bachelor’s (honours) degree with a final mark of **at least 65% or above**.
- If you have a lower degree classification, or a degree in an unrelated subject, your application may be considered if you can demonstrate **significant relevant work experience**, or offer a related graduate qualification such as a Masters or PGDip.
- **Programme specific requirements:** Undergraduate degree with high 2:1 honours, i.e. overall average of **at least 65% across all years of study**, required in a social or applied science such as finance, economics, management, engineering, applied mathematics, computer science or other relevant subject, or equivalent overseas qualification.
- The programme is most suitable if you have **some quantitative background in either finance and/or economics** or have a degree with some quantitative elements.
- If you are still studying, you should be achieving an average of **at least 65% or above** in the UK marking scheme.
- **China applicants:** Degree from Prestigious Institution: Award of Bachelor degree with an average score of **85%**, as evidenced by a Bachelor Degree Certificate and Final Transcripts with official English translations.
- **China applicants:** Degree from a Recognised Institution: Award of Bachelor degree with an average score of **88%**, as evidenced by a Bachelor Degree Certificate and Final Transcripts with official English translations.
- For postgraduate programmes within the King’s Business School and some programmes, offers will usually only be made to applicants from universities considered prestigious by UK ENIC at the point of assessment. A “prestigious institution” is one which is classified as by UK ENIC or within the Project 211/Double First Class list of institutions. You will be a stronger candidate for admission if you have high grades and are attending a university considered prestigious.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
English language band: **B**. To study at King's, you are usually required to provide certification of your competence in English before starting your studies. Nationals of majority English speaking countries ([as defined by the UKVI](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gov.uk%2Fstudent-visa%2Fknowledge-of-english&data=04%7C01%7Ccecily.peach%40kcl.ac.uk%7Cb4259f20b3944ff5d16d08d98e4ff7f6%7C8370cf1416f34c16b83c724071654356%7C0%7C0%7C637697296372923385%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIIiwibBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C1000&sdata=x12eNJmvgvrwW0WAWaGUYHH6T8ApelIW8aVXXI4froY%3D&reserved=0)) who have permanently resided in this country are not usually required to complete an additional English language test. This is also the case for applicants who have successfully completed an undergraduate degree (of at least three years duration), a postgraduate taught degree (of at least one year), or a PhD in a majority English speaking country ([as defined by the UKVI](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gov.uk%2Fstudent-visa%2Fknowledge-of-english&data=04%7C01%7Ccecily.peach%40kcl.ac.uk%7Cb4259f20b3944ff5d16d08d98e4ff7f6%7C8370cf1416f34c16b83c724071654356%7C0%7C0%7C637697296372933336%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIIiwibBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C1000&sdata=ah%2F%2FNnl5VP3nelM68z6oOMxxVD7vND1hwQ7cFYQetXg%3D&reserved=0)) within five years of the course start date.
Tests are valid if taken within **two years of the start date** of the chosen programme. For English language requirements, the start date is the 1st day of the month in which the programme commences; if the programme starts in September 2026, the test must be dated within two years of **1st September 2026**. All elements of the test results must be demonstrated in one test; King's cannot take a combination of scores across two tests, TOEFL MyBest scores, or IELTS One Skill scores.
- King's Pre-Sessional English language courses: **Pass with Band 7**.
- Cambridge Advanced Certificate (CAE)/Cambridge C1 Advanced: **185 overall; minimum 176 in all skills**.
- Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE)/Cambridge C2 Proficiency: **185 overall; minimum 176 in all skills**.
- IELTS (Academic): **7.0 overall with a minimum of 6.5 in each skill**.
- IELTS (Online): **7.0 overall with a minimum of 6.5 in each skill**.
- Oxford Test of English Advanced: **150 overall with 140 in each component**.
- Pearson Test of English (Academic): **69 overall with a minimum of 62 in each communicative skill**. King's also accepts Pearson Test of English (Academic) for UKVI, but does not accept Pearson Test of English (Academic) Online.
- TOEFL iBT or TOEFL iBT Home Editions, institution code **0394**: tests taken before **21 January 2026** require **100 overall with a minimum of 25 in writing and 23 in each of the other skills**; tests taken from **21 January 2026** require **5 overall with a minimum of 4.5 in each skill**.
- Trinity College London Integrated Skills in English (ISE): **Level III (ISEIII) with merit in each skill**.

Program Overview.content:
The world of finance is changing. With recent advances in technology, huge amounts of data are generated every second on a global scale. Finance professionals of the future will need to harness advanced technologies to process, analyse and ultimately extract key insights to tackle the challenges facing the industry. Students will acquire the knowledge and develop the skills and expertise needed for a broad range of careers in finance and other multinational organisations.
With a focus on big data analytics, the Finance Analytics MSc is designed to provide rigorous applied training in quantitative and empirical methods in Finance. This course is suited to individuals with strong quantitative backgrounds who desire the skills and expertise needed for a range of highly skilled technical professions in finance. Students study topics at the cutting edge of the finance industry such as data visualisation, big data, FinTech and robo-trading.
- Course type: Master's
- Delivery mode: In person
- Study mode: Full-time
- Duration: One year
- Credit value: 180
- Start date: September 2026
- Taught in: [King’s Business School](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/business "King’s Business School")
The Finance Analytics MSc course offers a combination of a rigorous academic programme that teaches the recent developments in data analytics and a unique practitioners’ view of how these developments are shaping the practical aspects of finance. The programme teaches big data methods with applications to risk management, product origination, and trading; text mining techniques with applications to forecasting; automation techniques with applications to robo-advice/trading; and FinTech developments in banking.
Graduates will gain knowledge and skills that are highly sought after by financial industry firms, including incumbent large financial institutions as well as disruptor/start-ups focusing on innovation. Given the importance of analytics in a broader context, the course also provides skills that can be used across a wide range of industries outside Finance, including e-commerce, hospitality, retail, pharmaceutical, and media.
Student employability is one of the main focuses of the Programme. The Programme has been designed in close collaboration with leading financial industry practitioners; active senior finance industry practitioners participate in the teaching of a large proportion of the modules; and the Programme offers additional ungraded modules that enhance students’ programming skills as well as their understanding of financial markets.
The course is most suitable for students with a background in finance, economics or business, or a degree with some quantitative elements. Located in the heart of London, King’s Business School has a strong reputation for research-led teaching and close links to the financial industry.
Base campuses include [Strand Campus](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/visit/strand-campus "Strand Campus") and [Waterloo Campus](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/visit/waterloo-campus "Waterloo Campus"). Locations are determined by where each module is taught and may vary depending on the modules studied.

Curriculum.content:
Courses are divided into modules. You will normally take modules totalling **180 credits**.
Required modules:
- Introduction to Analytics in Finance (15 credits)
- Principles of Finance (15 credits)
- Big Data Analytics and Visualisation (15 credits)
- Business Risk Analytics (15 credits)
- Dissertation (60 credits)
Optional modules:
- You are required to take 15 credits from: Big Data and Text Business and Finance Analytics (15 credits); FinTech Analytics and Robo Trading (15 credits); Conduct Risk Management (15 credits).
- You are required to take 45 credits from a range of optional modules that may typically include: Empirical Finance (15 credits); Corporate Finance (15 credits); Financial Econometrics (15 credits); Applied Behavioural Finance (15 credits); Portfolio Management (15 credits); Financial Derivatives for Data Analytics (15 credits); Mathematical Finance (15 credits); Risk Management for Data Analytics (15 credits).
Teaching methods:
| Module | Lectures, seminars and feedback | Self-study |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per 15-credit module | Between 20 and 30 hours which typically consist of a combination of lectures, case discussion and class activities; there may be some variation in the precise format. | Approximately 120-130 hours. |
| Dissertation module | Dissertation workshops and one-to-one supervision. | Approximately 595 hours self-study and project work. |
Typically, one credit equates to 10 hours of work. Face to face teaching will be complemented and supported with innovative technology so that students also experience elements of digital learning and assessment.
Assessment may typically include written examinations, coursework, individual or group projects, presentations, case studies and multiple-choice tests. Your performance will be assessed through a combination of coursework and written/practical examinations.
Key information: Course type: Master's. Delivery mode: In person. Study mode: Full-time. Duration: One year. Start date: September 2026.

Financial Aid.content:
King’s Business School offers postgraduate scholarships for master’s programmes (MSc), covering up to 50% tuition fees, and others worth up to £10,000.
- **Future Financial Leaders**: Scholarships up to **£10,000**. Available for successful applicants who demonstrate a passion for Finance and Economics, and plan to pursue a career in this field. Applicants should hold an offer for one of the listed courses, including **Finance Analytics MSc**.
- **Black & Ethnic Minority Scholarships**: Two scholarships covering **50% of fees**. Available for successful applicants who identify as belonging to specified Black or Mixed ethnic groups.
- **European Scholarships**: Scholarships up to **£10,000**. Available for successful applicants who are European nationals and can demonstrate academic excellence.
- **Future Sustainability Leaders**: Scholarships up to **£10,000**. Available for successful applicants who demonstrate a passion for and experience in sustainability and responsible business.
- **Global Scholarships**: Scholarships up to **£10,000**. Available for successful applicants who are nationals of countries outside of Europe; the School particularly welcomes applications from students in the Global South.
- **GREAT Scholarships**: Scholarships up to **£10,000**. Available for successful applicants who are passport holders from France, Greece, Italy, Spain, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. More information: [GREAT Scholarships 2026](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/business/postgraduate/great-scholarships).
- **King’s Community Scholarships**: Two scholarships covering **50% of fees**. Available for successful applicants who are alumni of King’s College London or current final year students at King’s College London seeking to further their studies at King’s Business School.
- **King's Business School - Trajetórias Scholarships**: Two scholarships up to **£10,000**. Available for successful Brazilian nationals who have satisfied the selection criteria set out by the Institute of Trajetórias and can demonstrate academic excellence.
- **UK Scholarships**: Scholarships up to **£10,000**. Available for successful UK nationals who can demonstrate academic excellence.
- **Vice Chancellor Awards**: Scholarships up to **£5000**. Available for India-domiciled offer holders. More information: [Vice Chancellor Awards](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/study-legacy/funding/vice-chancellors-awards-2026-27).
Scholarships are available for all full-time, in-person postgraduate courses. To be eligible, applicants must have received an offer for a postgraduate course at King’s Business School and provide their King’s Student Number. Applicants must complete a separate application form, including a short essay and video, and will be invited directly to apply once they receive an offer. Scholarship outcomes will be announced at the end of April 2026.
**Available to:** Offer holders
**Eligible programmes:** All full-time, in-person postgraduate courses
**Eligible fee status:** All
All scholarship opportunities have now closed.

Multiple Applications.content:
- Yes, you can apply for more than one course at King's. You may be required to pay multiple applications fees for each programme.
- If you receive offers for both, you will only be able to accept one of these.
- Once you have completed an online application you can click on “new application” and create another application for a different course.
- You cannot, however, make more than one application for the same course in an admissions cycle.
- If you decide to apply to more than one course which charges an application fee, you will need to pay for each application submitted.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
After careful consideration, King’s has taken the decision **not to allow any deferrals for postgraduate taught courses from the 2025/26 or 2026/27 academic year to future academic years**. King’s says it will announce whether it will permit deferrals from the 2027/28 academic year nearer the time.
Standard deferral guidance includes:
- King’s is unable to defer conditional offers; **all conditions must be met before King’s can defer your place**.
- If funding or a scholarship has been awarded for a specific academic year, there is no guarantee that same funding will be available after deferral, and applicants may have to re-apply for the academic year in which they intend to join.
- If a visa is required, the CAS and visa are assigned to a specific start date and course; if the start date changes, applicants [may have to apply for a new CAS or visa in the year that they wish to study](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/campuslife/services/student-advice-support/how/international-student-support/index).
- If the programme start date is deferred, fee status could be affected, and the Admissions Office reserves the right to re-assess fee status for the deferred start date.
- English language tests are only eligible for two years; if a deferral would make the English language test out of date, King’s reserves the right to amend the offer to a conditional offer based on demonstrating current proficiency with a new test.
- If accommodation, disability or dyslexia support arrangements have been made, applicants may need to re-apply or update arrangements for the new start date.
- For military service deferrals, **a deferral of two academic years** will usually only be considered if an applicant is completing compulsory national or military service which exceeds 12 months. Applicants need to provide evidence that they will be undertaking compulsory service with their deferral request, and all requests should be made via [King’s Apply](https://apply.kcl.ac.uk/).

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- Check if you need to meet any offer conditions to confirm your place at King’s and the deadline to meet these conditions.
- If you are given an offer which requires you to meet a condition(s) before your place can be confirmed, you will need to send King’s a message on King’s Apply using the “Meeting Offer Conditions/Confirmation” message category with evidence that you have met your conditions **by the deadline stated in your offer letter**.
- If you have an academic condition, King’s will need your final transcripts/certificates. The documentation must confirm that you have been awarded your qualification and the grade you have received to be accepted. If this is not in English, you must provide an official translation with the original.
- If you have an English Language condition, King’s will not accept scores that do not meet the requirements and cannot accept a combination of scores from multiple tests. If you are undertaking a pre-sessional English language programme with King’s to meet an English language condition, you should still meet any academic condition by the deadline in your offer letter; King’s will wait for the results of the pre-sessional course.
- If you have not met your academic condition, send your final documents to King’s; they will consider your application before making a final decision on whether your place can be confirmed on the programme.
- Remember if you have conditions to meet on your offer you will need to provide evidence of meeting these and any other requirements before the enrolment process can begin. **Failure to meet the stated deadlines may result in you losing your place on the course.**
